Almost no dialogue. Time must be visible as a number or a clock on screen or on the page
Second person. The visitor is addressed as if they are late
One location only. No flashbacks. Weather may change
Every section title is a timestamp. No other titles
Sentences may not be longer than 14 words
The locked character never explains themselves. Others may
Color may change only once, at the structural midpoint
No proper names except the locked ones. Everyone else is a job title
Include a running count of minutes wasted
All images (or image descriptions) must be of objects, never faces
The ending is already on the first screen in small type. The rest is how we got there
One joke allowed. It must be dry and not about slowness unless slowness is locked
No background music language. Sound only as onomatopoeia or UI beeps
Each page or section must reuse one sentence from the previous one, altered by a single word
The work must include a list that is wrong in one specific row
Mobile-first. If a website: desktop may not add information, only scale
Typographic contrast only. No photographs, no illustrations, no stock
The locked fact appears three times: mundane, official, and wrong
No question marks in the copy
Credits come first. The story is what remains after the names
No hero image. The first screen is type and one control
Every page must contain a number that is not decorative
Links may not say click here, read more, or learn more
The locked character is described only by what they handle, wear, or delay
English only, except one official word left untranslated
No shadows, no gradients, no blur
A footer exists and is part of the story, not legal fluff
If there is navigation, labels must be verbs
Do not mention the film, franchise, or studio unless those words are locked
One repeated object must appear in every section
Night and day may not both appear. Pick the one the draw implies
Any form control that is not needed for structure must be disabled and visible
